title: Categorize Products by SKU Pattern
description:
Write a query to classify every product by its SKU format and return the count per category.

SKUs fall into three categories:

| Category   | Format |
|------------|--------|
| `Standard` | Exactly two uppercase letters, a hyphen, then exactly four digits — e.g. `AB-1234` |
| `Bulk`     | One of `B`, `K`, or `G`, a hyphen, exactly three uppercase letters, then one digit — e.g. `K-ABC9` |
| `Other`    | Anything that does not match Standard or Bulk |

Return columns `sku_type` and `product_count`. Exclude categories with zero products. Order by `sku_type` ascending.
solutionSql:
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN REGEXP_LIKE(sku, '^[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{4}$') THEN 'Standard'
    WHEN REGEXP_LIKE(sku, '^[BKG]-[A-Z]{3}[0-9]$') THEN 'Bulk'
    ELSE 'Other'
  END AS sku_type,
  COUNT(*) AS product_count
FROM products
GROUP BY sku_type
ORDER BY sku_type;
hint: Put REGEXP_LIKE inside a CASE expression in the SELECT, then GROUP BY the same CASE expression. Evaluate the Standard pattern before Bulk so unambiguous SKUs are caught first.
outputExplanation:
- `AB-1234` — 2 uppercase letters, hyphen, 4 digits. `Standard`. ✓
- `K-ABC9` — `K` prefix, hyphen, 3 uppercase letters `ABC`, digit `9`. `Bulk`. ✓
- `B-AB12` — only 2 letters and 2 digits after the hyphen; fails both patterns. `Other`. ✗
- `XYZ-1` — 3 letters before the hyphen; Standard requires exactly 2. `Other`. ✗
- `$k-abc7` — starts with `$`; invalid for both patterns. `Other`. ✗
- `G-AAA0` — `G` prefix, hyphen, 3 uppercase letters `AAA`, digit `0`. `Bulk`. ✓

Final counts: Bulk = 2, Other = 3, Standard = 1.
